results.name: Encoding Challenge
results.attack: socket.cryptohack.org:13377, JSON-line protocol (pwntools-free raw socket). 100 levels of base64/hex/rot13/bigint/utf-8; decode per 'type' field, reply {"decoded": ...} each round; flag returned after level 100. Levels passed: 100/100 live.

results.name: Transparency
results.attack: Subdomain thetransparencyflagishere.cryptohack.org (previously derived via crt.sh against transparency.pem modulus). GET https://thetransparencyflagishere.cryptohack.org/ returns the flag as plain body (HTTP 200, fetched live twice). Note: the live TLS cert has since rotated (Let's Encrypt renewal), so current cert modulus no longer matches the 2020-era challenge PEM; flag endpoint is unchanged.

results.name: Let's Decrypt Again
results.attack: socket.cryptohack.org:13394. Server checks bytes_to_long(emsa_pkcs1_v15.encode(msg,96)) == pow(SIG,e,n) with attacker-chosen n (must be composite) and e. Recovered padding format by computing SIG^E mod N: 00 01 FF*58 00 || DigestInfo-SHA1(msg), 96 bytes. Chose n = q^52 with q=2010103 (prime, q-1 = 2*3*31*101*107 smooth, SIG verified primitive root mod q and SIG^(q-1) != 1 mod q^2, so SIG generates all of (Z/q^52)*); n = 2^1089 > digest. For each pattern msg (This is a test.../My name is.../valid P2SH BTC addr 3EovkHLK5kkAbE8Kpe53mkEbyQGjyf8ECw) + suffix, e = DLP_SIG(digest) mod n via pure-Python Pohlig-Hellman (CRT over prime-to-q part, 51-step BSGS lifting for the q-part). Three successful claims -> three shares -> XOR = flag. All three shares claimed in ONE live session.
